name: the first arrival fires; the same value does not; a different one does
a first arrival of undefined is NOT a change (lastValue starts undefined); null then is
because: valuechanged.ts :15, :32 — `undefined === undefined`; so the description says 'including the first time a value arrives' (P109 ISL-027, D9, ruled 'Reword the description'): undefined is not a value

name: -0 after 0 is not a change; two equal-looking objects are two changes (identity, not equality)
a primitive after a unit object arrives as sent, so a repeated 2 fires once, not on every write (ISL-026, C6)
because: was NSP-011 §6 C6 (R7): node.ts setInputValue merged a later value into a unit object on ANY port; since ISL-026 only a port whose type declares units merges; it minted a new { value: 2, unit } on every write, so a repeated 2 fired again
